primitives.name: Canvas Protection Isomorphism
primitives.verbatim_quote: Among the accessories it is customary to provide a square of canvas sufficiently large to cover the home plate and batsman's lines, and thus protect these lines during the practice preliminary to a game.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes rectangular canvas coverage, ignores curvature effects, treats field as planar.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when canvas stretches non-uniformly or when field terrain varies significantly.

layer2.mapping: Maps canvas coverage to conformal geometric protection, enabling GSI probability calibration and GSE state-transition safety.
layer2.telemetry: Measures canvas displacement relative to marked lines to detect field degradation.

primitives.name: Rubber Home Plate Substitution
primitives.verbatim_quote: The home plate is, by the rules, a whitened piece of rubber a foot square, sunk flush with the ground, its outer edges being within the lines to first and third bases.
primitives.assumptions: Treats rubber plate as a fixed reference point, assumes zero thickness for calculation purposes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when rubber deforms or erodes beyond acceptable tolerance levels.

layer2.mapping: Represents home plate as a Dirac delta function for GSI scoring models and a collision boundary for GSE trajectory analysis.
layer2.telemetry: Tracks plate elevation changes to infer wear patterns and rule violations.

primitives.name: Stuffed Canvas Bag Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: The first, second, and third bases are canvas bags, 15 inches square, stuffed with any soft material, and so fastened as to have their centers at the corners of the diamond which we have already marked out.
primitives.assumptions: Considers bags as rigid bodies with uniform density, neglects internal air pressure variations.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singular when stuffing compresses unevenly, causing asymmetric bounce.

layer2.mapping: Models bag impact dynamics as a Hertzian contact problem for GSE ball-bag collisions and as a latent variable in GSI player positioning uncertainty.
layer2.telemetry: Monitors bag deformation after high-velocity impacts to assess material fatigue.

primitives.name: Leather Strap Fastening Isomorphism
primitives.verbatim_quote: The customary method of fastening the bag is by means of a leather strap passing through loops upon the bag and directly around the center.
primitives.assumptions: Strap tension is constant, friction negligible, bag rotation prevented perfectly.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Degenerates when leather stretches plastically or loops tear.

layer2.mapping: Encapsulates fastening rigidity as a holonomic constraint in GSE kinematics and as a prior distribution in GSI error correction.
layer2.telemetry: Detects strap elongation via angle-of-attack sensors on the bag.
